standard_prerequisites.name: Length computed from a maximal chain
standard_prerequisites.use: Ties the number of steps of the chain to the length and forces the quotients to be simple.

standard_prerequisites.name: Multiplication by an element outside a maximal ideal is invertible
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used in the last part of the counted proof (the proof localises at a maximal ideal)
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that only the steps whose quotient is killed by that maximal ideal contribute to the localised length.

core_obligations: Show each quotient is simple, since otherwise the chain could be refined and would not be maximal (proof lines 12786-12788).
Read off from the length computation that the number of steps equals the length of M, and identify each simple quotient with the residue field of a maximal ideal (proof lines 12788 onward).
For a fixed maximal ideal, localise: a step contributes to the localised length exactly when its maximal ideal is the chosen one, which gives the stated counting identity (proof lines 12790-12816).
proof_roadmap: Use maximality to see the successive quotients are simple (proof lines 12785-12788).
Localise at a maximal ideal to count the steps with that residue field (proof lines 12788-12817).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a finite length module M and any maximal chain of submodules, the number of steps is the length of M, each successive quotient is simple of the form R modulo a maximal ideal, and the number of steps with a given maximal ideal equals the length of the localisation of M at it (statement lines 12762-12783). The proof does not compute with composition series abstractly: it first observes that a non-simple quotient would allow a refinement, then turns each simple quotient into a residue field, and finally localises at a single maximal ideal to isolate the steps belonging to it (proof lines 12785-12817). Locating the counting statement in the localised length is the step that carries the last part. H2.
